title: East Data, West Computing
summary: China's programme to move compute demand to western provinces with cheap power.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

Launched in February 2022, the initiative designates eight national computing hubs and ten clusters, concentrated in Guizhou, Gansu, Ningxia and Inner Mongolia, where electricity is cheap and land is abundant. The aim is to locate training and storage capacity away from coastal demand centres and to seed local industry. It is a planning instrument, so utilisation and latency economics vary widely by cluster.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Early commercial
Estimated window 2022–2025
Confidence label Confident
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

The lesson is that compute follows power pricing once latency tolerates distance; the same logic is now driving data-centre siting everywhere.

What Would Change The View

  • Actual utilisation of western clusters.
  • Interconnect capacity between west and east.
  • Whether AI training, rather than storage, anchors demand.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
